This is a fine example of why I oppose all the hue and cry over anthropogenic climate change - not because I believe that it doesn't exist (in fact, I argue that only a fool or a liar would claim that it doesn't exist), but because the constant companion to assertions of anthropogenic climate change is "and governments should be empowered to fix it," and I don't trust for even a second that governments so empowered actually would "fix" it.

I'm not convinced that they (or anyone else) could "fix" it anyway. The basis for my assertion that anthropogenic climate change exists is that climate is a staggeringly complex array of cause and effect in which countless causes have effects that ripple through the system, and human action - mere human existence - is self-evidently among those causes. It's impossible that human existence could not be a part of that system, therefore anthropogenic climate change - climate change resulting from human action - certainly exists. But the interplay of causes and effects is so complex that, at this particular point in time at least, it's simply impossible to map things accurately enough to know what causes lead to what effects, or what the full effects of some introduced cause might be, so I don't believe it's really possible, other than by chance, to "fix" any nominal problem, or at least to do so without making some other problem pop out somewhere else in that enormous web of cause and effect.

But that's really sort of irrelevant - my opposition is based on a much more fundamental point. Even in cases in which causes and effects can be fairly accurately understood, governments cannot be trusted to intervene responsibly, since government decisions are ALWAYS affected by the narrow self-interests of those who possess the authority to make the decisions. So even if climate was so simple and so fully understood that we could accurately chart the web of cause and effect and know for certain that this particular cause leads to this particular effect and that that particular change would have ONLY this particular effect, I still wouldn't trust any government to oversee it, since they still would be certain to manipulate the process to serve their own self-interest and the interests of their cronies and patrons, and thus to almost certainly defeat their own stated purpose.
